items.q: Is task switching the same as cognitive flexibility?
items.a: No — **cognitive flexibility** is broader. Task switching adds the start/stop cost of changing **operational mode**: the prefrontal cortex must **engage new circuits and disengage old ones**. You cannot flip instantly.

items.q: Why can't you drop into deep focus the second a new task starts?
items.a: Expect a **5–10 minute warm-up** on any non-trivial task. Instant focus on a awaited text is high **salience**, not proof your attention is broken — immediate deep focus on boring/new material is biologically unrealistic.

items.q: How short can a useful transition between tasks be?
items.a: Even **15 seconds** labeled "transition" improves engagement on task B — count **10→1** or **1→10**. Gap duration scales with prior depth: light email → seconds–**2 min**; deep grant writing → up to **5–10 min** if available.

items.q: What is the worst common transition mistake?
items.a: Checking your **phone between tasks** — photos and video create a high-stimulus **hidden third task**. "Please don't introduce yet more tasks. Switching from one task to another is hard enough already."

items.q: How many cognitively heavy goals should you set per day?
items.a: Use the Berkeley professor method: write **1–3 critical tasks** — never more. Everything else runs on automaticity; **exercise and social life stay off the list** of cognitively demanding goals.

items.q: What ~2-minute drill trains the brain to shift time domains?
items.a: **Space-time bridging**: eyes closed (interoception) → hand surface → ~**10 ft** → ~**50 ft** → horizon → close eyes return; **~5–15 s** per station. Huberman does it daily ~**2 min** to train the near/far shifts task switching needs.

items.q: Does this public AMA cover the brain-fog protocols in the title?
items.a: The free YouTube cut focuses almost entirely on **task-switching tools** plus a Premium pitch. **Brain-fog protocols** are promised in the full Premium AMA but are **not in the available public transcript**.
